svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A sarcomere: the repeating unit of a myofibril in skeletal muscle."], [1.5, "A nerve impulse releases Ca\u00b2\u207a ions; tropomyosin moves and exposes binding sites on actin."], [3, "Myosin heads bind to actin (cross-bridges) and pivot: the power stroke pulls actin towards the M line."], [5, "ATP binds, the heads detach; ATP is hydrolysed to re-cock them, and the cycle repeats."], [9, "The sarcomere shortens: the I band and H zone get shorter; the A band stays the same. The filaments slide; they do not shorten."]]
svg.title: The sliding filament model
svg.desc: A sarcomere with Z lines, actin and myosin, M line, I band, A band and H zone; animated cross-bridge cycling slides actin over myosin so the sarcomere, I band and H zone shorten while the A band stays the same.
svg.text: Muscle contraction: the sliding filament model
One sarcomere, simplified (lengths not to scale).

g.data-info: Mark the ends of each sarcomere; actin filaments are anchored to them.
Twisted protein strands with tropomyosin and troponin. Binding sites for myosin are covered at rest.
Bundles of myosin molecules with heads that bind actin and pull: the cross-bridges.
The centre of the sarcomere, where the myosin filaments are held together.
The whole length of the myosin filaments: dark band. It stays the same length.
Myosin only, in the centre. It gets shorter, and may disappear, during contraction.
Actin only: light band. It gets shorter during contraction.
Actin only: light band. It gets shorter during contraction.

svg.text: sarcomere (Z line to Z line) shortens

g.text: actin slides towards the M line
